sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar Tripathi,Ajeet Kumar Singh,Vijay Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.

The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.326 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B,
34/302 of IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Behta Gokul, District Hardoi.
3. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the sister of the informant was married to the applicant on 11.05.2022 and sufficient dowry was also given.
It was also alleged that the applicant and the other family members beaten her sister on 16.06.2022 and left at his house on account of non-fulfillment of dowry.

sentences.text: 4. In the light of the aforesaid, the Counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the postmortem report, which indicates the cause of death as ante mortem handing
and apart from the ligature mark, two abrasions were found on elbow joint and left foot, which according to the applicant arose at the time of bring the body down.
5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

6. Considering the fact that there is no allegation against the applicant, who is the husband, to suggest that soon before her death, the victim was subjected to any physical or mental harassment in relation to any demand of dowry coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 22.06.2022, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Saheeq be released on bail in the abovesaid first information report number on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
